practice_items.prompt: A host on VLAN 10 wants to send data to a host on VLAN 20. What device must the traffic pass through?
options: A hub
A router or layer-3 switch
Another VLAN-tagged host
The same switch port
practice_items.explain: VLANs are separate broadcast domains. Traffic crossing VLANs must pass through a router (inter-VLAN routing) where firewall rules are applied.

practice_items.prompt: Which of the following are TRUE about VLANs? Select ALL that apply.
options: VLANs are logical, not physical, separations
A single switch can host multiple VLANs simultaneously
VLANs prevent all forms of attack with no additional configuration
Broadcast traffic on one VLAN is not visible to hosts on a different VLAN
practice_items.explain: VLANs are logical, one switch supports many, and broadcasts are confined per VLAN. VLANs alone do not prevent attacks, firewall rules at the routing boundary are also required.

practice_items.prompt: An attacker compromises a guest device on the visitor VLAN. The corporate file server is on the server VLAN. Assuming correct VLAN configuration and restrictive firewall rules, what can the attacker reach from the guest device?
options: The file server and all other internal servers
Only trunk ports
Any device on any VLAN because they share the same switch
Only devices on the same guest VLAN; the file server is unreachable
practice_items.explain: Segmentation confines the attacker to their VLAN. The file server is in a different VLAN and the router/firewall blocks cross-VLAN access to internal servers from the guest VLAN.

practice_items.prompt: What is the purpose of a trunk port?
options: To block all VLAN traffic
To carry 802.1Q-tagged frames for multiple VLANs on a single physical link
To connect an end-user workstation to exactly one VLAN
To assign IP addresses to hosts
practice_items.explain: Trunk ports carry frames tagged with VLAN IDs (802.1Q), allowing multiple VLANs to share an uplink between a switch and a router.

practice_items.prompt: Name the attack technique where an intruder who has compromised one host attempts to reach additional hosts deeper in the network.
practice_items.explain: Lateral movement (also called pivoting) is the technique of moving from one compromised host to another. Segmentation limits it by requiring the attacker to break through a new access control boundary at each VLAN boundary.

practice_items.prompt: What is the core paradigm of a Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA)?
options: Never trust, always verify, regardless of where the connection request originates
Implicit trust is granted once a device successfully authenticates to the VPN
Trust but verify internal hosts based on their physical network connection
Trust all devices connected to the internal Management VLAN
practice_items.explain: Zero Trust assumes that all network traffic is untrusted by default, whether it originates from outside the perimeter or inside the local network. It requires explicit, continuous verification.

practice_items.prompt: Which of the following are core practices of a Zero Trust Network Architecture? Select ALL that apply.
options: Verifying device health and compliance posture before granting resource access
Permitting unlimited lateral movement within the server VLAN
Using microsegmentation to limit the blast radius of a breach
Granting broad access privileges based on physical location in the office
practice_items.explain: Zero Trust relies on explicit posture verification and microsegmentation. It removes implicit trust based on network location or physical presence, and blocks unrestricted lateral movement.

practice_items.prompt: In a Private VLAN (PVLAN) setup, what type of port is completely blocked from communicating with any other ports in the same PVLAN, except for promiscuous ports?
options: Community port
Isolated port
Trunk port
Secondary port
practice_items.explain: Isolated ports in a Private VLAN cannot communicate with other isolated ports or community ports. They can only send and receive traffic from promiscuous ports (typically routers or gateways).

practice_items.prompt: Name the security technique that applies fine-grained security policies to individual hosts or workloads, treating each device as its own isolated boundary to limit lateral movement.
practice_items.explain: Microsegmentation divides the network into fine-grained zones, down to individual hosts or application containers, to prevent unauthorized east-west (lateral) traffic.
